reference_meta.coverage_note: ~98%. Page opens mid-word ('flam-mam fugiunt'): the subject 'those bodies which' is on the previous page. reference_meta.title: The Narrative of Alvar Nuñez Cabeça de Vaca (in Spanish Explorers in the Southern United States, 1528-1543, ed. F. W. Hodge, 1907)
reference_meta.translates_edition: La relacion y comentarios (Valladolid 1555) — the text family of this scan ('frisoles y calabazas', not 1542 'melones')
reference_meta.located: Chapter 30, from 'The sick having recovered...' to 'Thus they boil their food.' + Chapter 31 heading (Gutenberg #42841)
reference_meta.coverage_note: Page = second half of ch. 30 from its paragraph start, plus the ch. 31 heading; reference covers the same span in order. Hodge's footnotes and markers stripped. Smith adds 'after talking with the Indians, Castillo returned at the end of three days' where the scan's OCR line is garbled ('Aquí llegaron Castillo y Estebanico adonde nos había dejado'); Smith's 'otherwise in a journey of seventeen days' differs in logic from the Spanish ('en diez y siete jornadas no hallaríamos...'); 'mayor viveza y habilidad' -> 'greatest activity and strength'.

reference_meta.title: Theologia Germanica (Golden Treasury reprint of the 1854 translation)
reference_meta.translates_edition: Franz Pfeiffer's edition (1851) of the Würzburg 1497 manuscript text; our book is the Luther-line Basel 1523 print, whose chapter XXXI = Winkworth's ch. XXXIII
reference_meta.located: End of ch. XXXII and start of ch. XXXIII, pp. 116-119 of the 1893 reprint, from 'So it is good and just and right to deem' to 'for I am and have nothing else'
reference_meta.coverage_note: Page starts mid-sentence ('[were icht] bessers dann gott, das müst geliebt werden vor gott'), so the whole English sentence is included. The page ends mid-sentence at 'gleich als gott auß der menscheit [sprech]'; the whole English sentence, i.e. God's quoted speech (on the next page in the German), is included to its end. The source's stray 'Vñ Got liebt sich' at the end of the first line (likely a printed running gloss/catchphrase) has no separate English. Winkworth adds a chapter title ('How when a Man is made truly Godlike...') that the 1523 print gives only as a margin summary ('Natur und eygenschafft der rechten liebe, die sich erstrecket allein und fürnemlich zu unsern feynden'); the two margin glosses are not otherwise rendered. Winkworth's 'and rejoice in their welfare', 'Thou desirest and rejoicest in My affliction' are small expansions of the German.

reference_meta.title: The Perfumed Garden of the Cheikh Nefzaoui: A Manual of Arabian Erotology (XVI. Century). Revised and corrected translation
reference_meta.translator: Sir Richard F. Burton (attrib.; Kama Shastra Society), from the French version of 'Baron R***' (1876)
reference_meta.licence_detail: Public Domain (privately printed, Cosmopoli/Benares 1886; Burton d. 1890)
reference_meta.located: Ch. 9 'Names given to the sexual organs of women', story of Abu Nuwas' friend and Fadehat el Djemal, pp. 154–156 of the 1886 ed.
reference_meta.coverage_note: INDIRECT translation: Burton's English renders the French version, made from a different Arabic recension, not this Gafsa manuscript. Content and order diverge: the reference puts the vulva description before the kiss (the MS has the face shining like lightning 'when the stallion drew near' and the white/red 'pistachio' description at the page end); oaths differ ('son of a debauched woman' vs 'son of a whore', 'religion of my father' vs 'by the right of your mother'); the reference adds phrases absent from the page (crystal tinged with carmine, superiors and masters). The page's 'like a well' and lightning simile are not rendered. Roughly 70% of the page's content is covered.
reference_meta.source_edition: French translation by 'Baron R***' (Algiers/Paris 1876, Liseux reprint), from an Arabic MS other than this one

reference_meta.coverage_note: Reference covers the whole root text on the page. The page ends at 中德 mid-sentence. Marginal glosses (旁注) have no reference. reference_meta.title: 大乘起信論義記(二) (vol 2)
reference_meta.located: Awakening of Faith, the six coarse aspects (六麤): aspect 2 相續相 (whole) and the beginning of aspect 3 執取相
reference_meta.coverage_note: Wording 依於智故生其苦樂覺心起念相應不斷故 matches Paramartha's T1666, which Richard translated. Richard's rendering is free: aspect 1 'Consciousness' (context, not on page), aspect 2 'Emotion' (= 相續相, on page), aspect 3 'Attention' (= 執取相, beginning on page). Two OCR misreadings in the archive.org text were corrected: '(6.)' -> '(b.)' and the comma before 'These' -> full stop. Fazang's commentary (most of the page) has no reference.
